name: phase1_instruction_table
description: Does the instruction consuming an operand matter, once the operand has to
move to reach it?
This is the last experiment Phase 1 needs, and the last item of the plan's
original Phase 1 that survives. It cannot be run the way that plan wrote
it. The register-resident instruction victims do not leak at all -- an
avx2_mul contrast lands at the harness noise floor -- so a per-instruction
table built on them would be a table of noise. The ws_op_* victims put the
same instructions behind the ws_l3_x8 load stream instead: 8 x 32-byte
loads per iteration from a 4M working set, then 8 independent operations on
what was loaded.
The load stream is byte-for-byte identical across the family and the loop
is load-bound with margin, so every variant moves operands at the same rate
and the instruction is the only thing that varies. A pre-flight measured
134-142 GB/s across all nine variants against 140 GB/s for loads alone --
within 4%, with no ALU-bound outlier, and full rate for fma and vnni in
particular, so no microcode assist fires on the NaN operand. The GB/s
column in the results is the standing check; pJ/byte corrects it if a
variant ever does fall off.
Both source registers of each operation are the same loaded register, which
makes the result Hamming weight predictable. For an operand v broadcast
through the buffer, op(v, v) gives:
victim      instruction     result        result HW at 0 / 0xFFFFFFFF
op_mov      vmovdqa         v             0 / 32
op_and      vpand           v             0 / 32
op_or       vpor            v             0 / 32
op_xor      vpxor           0             0 / 0
op_shift    vpsllvd         v << v        0 / 0   (a shift of >= 32)
op_add      vpaddd          2v            0 / 31
op_mul      vpmuludq        v * v         0 / 32 per 64-bit lane
op_fma      vfmadd231ps     accumulated   +0.0f / NaN
op_vnni     vpdpbusd        accumulated   0 / dot product of 0xFF bytes
So op_and and op_or against op_xor and op_shift is the input-versus-output
contrast, and it is nearly free: identical input traffic, same instruction
cost class, and a result that either tracks the operand or is pinned at
zero whatever the operand is. If the leakage is entirely input-driven the
four agree. If the result contributes, the first two sit above the last
two. This is the cheap form of the plan's operand-HW-versus-result-HW item;
the expensive form needs a store path and is only worth building if this
shows something.
Predictions. Section 3 of the chapter found that register-resident operands
do not leak, but it established that for vpmuludq alone. If that
generalises, every row here should land on loads_only (+2.05 W in the depth
sweep) and the table's result is a *bound*: instruction identity contributes
less than the resolution against a 2 W movement term. That would be a real
result, and the one most consistent with everything else in this chapter.
The rows that could break it are op_fma and op_vnni. vpmuludq is a modest
integer unit; an FMA on NaN against +0.0, or an int8 dot product over 0xFF
bytes against zero bytes, drives far more switching inside the execution
unit itself. reg_fma and reg_vnni are the controls that would separate 'the
ALU leaks' from 'the ALU leaks only when its operands also move': they run
the same two instructions register-resident, where section 3 predicts a
null.
Four repeats rather than three. The differences of interest here are
between rows that share a large common term, and at ~2 W the between-run SD
is ~0.10 W, so three repeats resolve a row-to-row difference of about
0.16 W and four resolve about 0.14 W.
loads_only is ws_l3_x8 on the same contrast measured in three earlier
sessions (+2.054 W depth_l3, +1.841 W l3_forward, +1.904 W hw32), so it is
the baseline row and the session anchor at once.

runs.label: aa_op
runs.comment: A/A gate on the new victim family. Predict 0.

runs.label: loads_only
runs.comment: No ALU work. Baseline row and session anchor; predict ~+2.0 W.

runs.label: op_and
runs.comment: vpand. Result HW tracks the operand.

runs.label: op_or
runs.comment: vpor. Result HW tracks the operand.

runs.label: op_xor
runs.comment: vpxor. Result pinned at 0 in both conditions.

runs.label: op_shift
runs.comment: vpsllvd. Result also 0 in both conditions; a second output-pinned row.

runs.label: op_add
runs.comment: vpaddd. Result 2v, HW 31 at the ones operand.

runs.label: op_mul
runs.comment: vpmuludq. The instruction the whole project started from.

runs.label: op_fma
runs.comment: vfmadd231ps. +0.0f against NaN; the widest ALU switching in the set.

runs.label: op_vnni
runs.comment: vpdpbusd. The int8 dot product quantised ML inference issues.

runs.label: reg_fma
runs.comment: Register-resident control for op_fma. Section 3 predicts a null.

runs.comment: Register-resident control for op_vnni. Section 3 predicts a null.
